name: Arnav Khandelwal
positioning: I build backends and AI pipelines that are fast, auditable and honest about their numbers.
bio: I'm Arnav Khandelwal, an Electrical Engineering undergraduate at MNIT Jaipur. I build backend applications, REST APIs and AI-enabled systems in Python and Java.

During a 2026 backend internship, I worked on an offline FastAPI telemetry service: request validation, structured responses, retries and reproducible local deployment. Its public benchmark captures the impact of a localhost DNS fix.

My work spans cited research agents, deterministic reconciliation, a bounded desktop guide and experimental brain-response inference. I care about debugging the mechanism and making the evidence inspectable.

projects.title: Project Edge Node
projects.descriptor: Offline telemetry, measured end to end.
projects.summary: A local telemetry classifier with validated inputs, structured output and a documented localhost latency fix.
projects.problem: Classify workplace telemetry without sending it to a hosted model, while keeping responses predictable and local execution reproducible.
approach: Validate requests with Pydantic and translate telemetry into prose for the local model.
Constrain model output with a JSON schema; retry invalid responses with corrective feedback and expose structured failures.
Benchmark latency, time to first token and memory, then replace IPv6-first localhost resolution with 127.0.0.1.
projects.result: The committed report records mean latency decreasing from 5.356s to 0.973s, with 50 latency requests and zero failures. Time to first token was measured separately over 10 requests.
limits: Results describe the repository benchmark environment, not a general guarantee across hardware.
Workplace classifications are model outputs, not a clinical assessment.

figure.caption: Mean end-to-end request latency in seconds. Source: committed benchmark report; 50 latency requests.

projects.title: Cited Multi-Agent Researcher
projects.summary: A research pipeline that scales search effort to the question and keeps citations attached to its synthesis.
projects.problem: Produce an answer whose sources can be inspected without running an expensive fixed-size agent team for every question.
approach: Classify the query as fact or comparison and decompose it into search tasks.
Run independent search agents concurrently, with a cap of five; deduplicate sources and assign stable citation identifiers.
Stream synthesis over server-sent events and evaluate factuality and citation coverage with a judge.
projects.result: The public README documents up to five concurrent search agents and a 33-unit-test suite. A separate résumé timing claim is excluded until a public benchmark is committed.
limits: A citation is inspectable evidence, not proof that every generated claim is correct.
The judge is an LLM evaluation and must not be read as independently verified factual accuracy.

projects.title: LedgerBridge
projects.descriptor: Deterministic reconciliation. Evidence for every exception.
projects.summary: An auditable bank, ledger and Razorpay reconciliation engine with deterministic matching and a read-only narration layer.
projects.problem: Reconcile financial records while preserving the rule, evidence and unresolved exceptions behind each decision.
approach: Run indexed matching passes with Decimal arithmetic and explicit ambiguity handling.
Classify unresolved records with an exception taxonomy and preserve input, configuration and engine hashes in the audit trail.
Keep optional model narration separate from matching authority; publish demo, sealed and scale evaluations with their limitations.
projects.result: The README reports 103,049 records processed in 5.114s median engine time over five runs. Its sealed-benchmark consistency scores are explicitly not real-world accuracy.
limits: The published benchmark uses project datasets and is not production financial reconciliation performance.
Specification consistency on a sealed benchmark is not real-world matching accuracy.

figure.title: Every record gets a disposition.
figure.caption: Demo dataset: 77 records, 62 matched, 15 evidenced exceptions. Scale timings use a separate dataset.

projects.title: GhostCursor
projects.descriptor: An AI desktop guide that waits for you.
projects.summary: A bounded local Windows assistant that highlights a trusted control, waits for a human action and verifies the resulting state.
projects.problem: Help users complete unfamiliar desktop workflows without giving a model unrestricted execution authority.
approach: Map goals to registered intents and reviewed, digest-bound recipes rather than model-generated coordinates or code.
Observe the current application, highlight one trusted control and wait for the human to act.
Verify the new state and measure raw model intent accuracy separately from authorized execution.
projects.result: The public README reports 27/30 raw intent accuracy on its frozen test set and 361 hermetic tests. These describe the documented supported-workflow evaluation.
limits: Support is limited to the reviewed recipes and tested Windows workflows.
The 30-case intent set is small; its accuracy does not establish performance on arbitrary software.

figure.title: The human keeps execution authority.
figure.caption: The guide observes and verifies; the human performs the action.

projects.title: NeuroUX
projects.descriptor: Brain-response inference on a laptop GPU.
projects.summary: An experimental media-analysis pipeline that maps predicted cortical activation to transparent UX scoring formulas.
projects.problem: Run a large brain-prediction model on a 4 GB laptop GPU and turn its outputs into an inspectable application.
approach: Use TRIBE v2 to predict cortical activation and aggregate it into 12 atlas regions.
Load text weights in 4-bit NF4 and move the video encoder to the GPU in fp16.
Fix scoring ties by preserving activation magnitude before region-level normalization; expose regional scores and comparisons in the UI.
projects.result: The README reports video inference changing from 50 minutes to approximately 80 seconds after moving the encoder to GPU. This is a reported engineering observation, not a controlled benchmark.
limits: The UX and virality formulas are experimental proxies, not validated predictions of actual audience behavior.
Reported timing is approximate and hardware-specific; the text-inference estimates are excluded because the README mixes estimated and observed baselines.
Without model weights, the application uses a deterministic stub; stub output is not neuroscience inference.

figure.title: Make inference fit the machine.
figure.caption: Repository-reported video timing: 50 minutes to approximately 80 seconds; hardware-specific observation.

projects.title: StudyOS
projects.descriptor: Learn next. Ask in context. Remember.
projects.summary: A learning workflow connecting prerequisite-aware next topics, contextual questions and spaced review.
projects.problem: Keep learning momentum when the next topic is unclear, questions arise outside the dashboard and useful answers disappear.
approach: Prioritize the next curriculum topic using prerequisites, progress and due reviews.
Use the Point & Ask extension to ask about selected text or a region, without sending the entire page by default.
Save useful answers for spaced review and gate the AWS delivery pipeline with tests, type checks and builds.
projects.result: The public repository documents Today → Point & Ask → Save to Review and an AWS deployment pipeline. No learning-outcome or adoption metric is claimed.
limits: The repository does not report measured learning outcomes or user adoption.
A documented deployment is not evidence that the public demo is currently available.
Team composition and individual contribution boundaries have not been confirmed.
